# Colour and light

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Grounds, living light, key light and shadows, accent timing, grades and colour changes that carry meaning. 59 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Light lines shoot through the frame

`dv-light-line-shoot` · opening hooks · signature · energy high · launch, sting

From black, a thin light bar shoots up from the frame edge to full height in a few frames; lines extend from a hero to the corners; thin light axes pierce an object one after another.

- **Build:** Build: <LightLine at from to color width> (fx/Streak): grows from from on E.snapOut (12 f) and thins to 35 % (10 f); stagger several 10-30 f apart for axes; flat by default, soft adds a static blurred copy on dark stages. Anatomy: Bar 60-100 px wide with a 20-30 px soft edge, or 2 px lines; grow from an edge or a point; thin afterwards. Sound: The first music hit right after.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Streak.LightLine`
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** Bar 12 f quad-out (peak 462 px/f); lines 5-8 f; axes 10-30 f apart.
- **Use when:** A cold open on a dark stage; a hero moment in a 3D world.
- **Avoid when:** Neon glows (keep the lines thin and the halo small).

### Brand colour withheld until the mark lands

`dv-brand-colour-last` · logo and end card · workhorse · energy calm · launch, sting

The mark stays white or ink until everything has cooled, then switches to the brand colour in one frame; or the wordmark is re-coloured for each background and lands on the brand colour last.

- **Build:** HardStep on the mark's fill. Anatomy: One-frame switch; a stepped colour sequence per background. Sound: The switch 157 ms after a beat. Materials: Over a warm plate the white wordmark first turns the plate's complement for 4 f (it reads as a translucent multiply), then the brand colour fills the letters from the bottom up with a hard, unfeathered boundary (half, then full, one step every 2 f); the mark switches 2 f before the letters.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Materials:** Over a warm plate the white wordmark first turns the plate's complement for 4 f (it reads as a translucent multiply), then the brand colour fills the letters from the bottom up with a hard, unfeathered boundary (half, then full, one step every 2 f); the mark switches 2 f before the letters.
- **Timing:** 1 f switch; 8 f in 4 steps.
- **Use when:** End cards and lockups.
- **Avoid when:** A brand colour that is already everywhere in the film.

### A light sheen crosses a landing object once

`dv-sheen-pass` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · any

A soft pale band about 1.5 letters wide crosses the end logo or a turning object once; mirrored highlights glide along an object's rims; a title fades up with a light sweep and a 1.2-1.4x brightness overshoot.

- **Build:** <LightSweep band={0.45} frames={34}> clipped to the element; rims: LightSweep clipped to the stroke. Recipe: the rounded rect stroked twice with a bright dash (strokeDasharray 120 of 1000) moving in opposite directions from the end, plus a blurred glow copy. Anatomy: Band 0.45 of the element width moving at about 24 px/f; rim variant: two short streaks mirrored about the centre, front-loaded then linear. Sound: The final kick after the sweep. Materials: A bright C-shaped end cap on a glass pill's rounded end (peak luma 150-200 on a dark panel, glow about 10 px) holds 12 f, then divides: one highlight runs along the top rim and one along the bottom for about 40 f, like light rolling off a glass edge.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure.LightSweep`
- **Materials:** A bright C-shaped end cap on a glass pill's rounded end (peak luma 150-200 on a dark panel, glow about 10 px) holds 12 f, then divides: one highlight runs along the top rim and one along the bottom for about 40 f, like light rolling off a glass edge.
- **Timing:** 26-48 f near-linear (rim: fast start 39 px/f then 15-28 px/f).
- **Use when:** An end logo landing, a hero object turning, a title reveal.
- **Avoid when:** Repeating sheens; a sheen on every element.

### A photo turned into a two- or three-ink gradient map

`dv-gradient-map-plate` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, vertical

A photograph (clouds, a landscape, a soft figure) is mapped by luminance onto the film's inks: shadows to the deep ink, mids to the accent, highlights to a pale tint, so real imagery carries the brand palette; the map can hold or drift slowly (a head turning from one ink to the next).

- **Build:** Photo with a gradeFilter table built from the brand stops (SVG feComponentTransfer); a drifting map = two statically filtered copies cross-faded by opacity, never an animated filter. Anatomy: Desaturate, then a three-stop table per channel (dark, mid, light); an optional blur (12-30 px) for a defocused figure; slow drift about 2 px/f; optional tiny specks and soft horizontal glints over a two-ink field. Sound: Music; no sound of its own. Materials: Two-ink field: luminance 0 -> deep ink, 0.5 -> accent, 1 -> pale tint. Infrared: swap the red and green channels so foliage turns crimson while the sky stays blue. Defocused figure: blur 30 px, then a four-stop map whose head and body stops drift apart.
- **Primitive:** `fx/GradientMap.GradientMap`
- **Materials:** Two-ink field: luminance 0 -> deep ink, 0.5 -> accent, 1 -> pale tint. Infrared: swap the red and green channels so foliage turns crimson while the sky stays blue. Defocused figure: blur 30 px, then a four-stop map whose head and body stops drift apart.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Holds a whole shot; a drifting map changes its stops over 30-100 f with no snaps.
- **Use when:** Real imagery that must live in a strong palette; an opening field; an infrared or thermal flavour for vision and generation products.
- **Avoid when:** Faces that must read naturally; product screenshots.

### Background steps back behind the type

`dv-background-veil` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · any

The picture behind a line gets a pale haze and a defocus, a canvas fades into a blurred image, a colour field fades to the neutral stage under the UI, or a dark vignetted plate puts the headline in the bright centre.

- **Build:** <RackFocus levels> on the background with a veil layer; vignette as a static plate. Anatomy: Background luma lifted (151 -> 224) and defocused; or a vignette with corners at a third of the centre. Sound: None. Materials: Calm, uncanny photoreal plates (a lone chair in a meadow, a misty window) in one cool grade carry the copy: an elliptical vignette about 45 % darker at the corners, a lift behind the type, saturation about 0.7; the plates creep almost imperceptibly (0.02-0.4 % a frame) while the copy changes on them.
- **Primitive:** `fx/RackFocus`
- **Materials:** Calm, uncanny photoreal plates (a lone chair in a meadow, a misty window) in one cool grade carry the copy: an elliptical vignette about 45 % darker at the corners, a lift behind the type, saturation about 0.7; the plates creep almost imperceptibly (0.02-0.4 % a frame) while the copy changes on them.
- **Timing:** 30-38 f; a fade 23 f sine.
- **Use when:** Type over footage or a busy picture.
- **Avoid when:** Dark drop shadows behind type.

### Drain the stage, keep the hero

`cl-drain-stage-keep-hero` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

Everything around the hero fades and the world drops to dark or bleaches to white, while the hero stays crisp in place, isolating it or closing a section.

- **Build:** Duplicate the hero onto a top layer at identical coordinates so nothing under it can shift. Isolate: fade the rest of the layer to 0 on E.linear to reveal a mid-grey plate, then mix the plate from C.mist toward C.ink2 on E.in (world luma from about 238 to 87) while the hero gains a 20 px radius and a soft shadow; in a light film, drain the surroundings to C.white instead and assemble the next page around the parked hero. Focus variant: render the side columns through RackFocus (t 0 to 1, blur 8; never an animated blur filter on the columns) and drop them to 0.6 opacity while the centre stays untouched and the parent scales from 1 to 1.06. Exhale: after a peak, or once the lockup has held 90-120 f, dim the stage first (stage opacity 1 to 0, or brightness 1 to 0.6 during a push-in) and fade the hero 8 f later, ending on a hard cut mid-film or on a short C.ink tail only at the very end.
- **Timing:** Neighbours fade over 12 f on E.linear, the world dims over 10 f on E.in, then hold about 30 f. A white drain takes 6-16 f on E.linear. Column focus takes 18 f on E.smooth. In the exhale, the stage fades over 36 f and the hero over 30 f starting 8 f later, with a tail of up to 22 f; a push-in dim takes 8 f on E.in.
- **Use when:** Search results, a found item, a selected post or row, the moment before a detail view, and the ends of sections or of the film.
- **Avoid when:** The hero itself must move during the isolation, or the neighbours carry context the viewer still needs.

### Floor glow under the stage, brightening into reveals

`dv-floor-glow` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · any

A one-hue glow rises from the bottom 25-30 % of the frame under UI or type; it brightens into reveals and transitions, can undulate in soft lobes, and is stronger on the end card.

- **Build:** <LightField floor={{ plate, height: 0.27, breathe, rises }}>. Bake each stop set with scripts/dither-gradient.py (kind floor) and move the plates by transform; never an animated CSS gradient. Anatomy: Bottom band luma rising 4 -> 189 into a reveal; lobes slowly undulating; strength stepping up on the end card. Sound: A sub-bass hit on the rise; an outro pad under the sink. Materials: The floor glow is a horizon at dusk, not one colour: a near-white core with a cool tint at the very bottom edge, then the accent body, a deeper hue and a fade to black (radial ellipse about 140 % of the frame wide and 60 % tall, centred just below the frame); it rises over about 68 f as the panel rises. The closing version is a row of 4-5 soft lobes along the bottom third (500-700 px wide, blur about 80 px) with darker gaps, rising and falling out of phase (20-40 px, 2-4 s periods) and sinking 300 px in 30 f before the logo. A three-hue aurora can rise under a translucent prompt box (coverage 2 -> 28 % of the panel in 48 f, then breathing 25-35 %, its core drifting and tilting about 20 deg), visible through the box's lower third.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Materials:** The floor glow is a horizon at dusk, not one colour: a near-white core with a cool tint at the very bottom edge, then the accent body, a deeper hue and a fade to black (radial ellipse about 140 % of the frame wide and 60 % tall, centred just below the frame); it rises over about 68 f as the panel rises. The closing version is a row of 4-5 soft lobes along the bottom third (500-700 px wide, blur about 80 px) with darker gaps, rising and falling out of phase (20-40 px, 2-4 s periods) and sinking 300 px in 30 f before the logo. A three-hue aurora can rise under a translucent prompt box (coverage 2 -> 28 % of the panel in 48 f, then breathing 25-35 %, its core drifting and tilting about 20 deg), visible through the box's lower third.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Rise 68 f ease-out; continuous breathing; sinks 32 f at the end.
- **Use when:** Dark or near-white product stages that should not be flat.
- **Avoid when:** Glow behind a single element; saturated glow.

### Ground colour changes per shot and per act

`dv-ground-alternation` · colour and light · workhorse · energy medium · any

The ground itself is a beat: shots alternate paper, black with a fine grid, a full brand field, a texture; an act flips the film from a light stage to a dark world and stays there; brand moments sit on a warm stage and the product on a cool one.

- **Build:** Recipe: a GROUNDS list in the timeline indexed by shot; the flip is a hard cut. Anatomy: A ground per shot from a set of 3-5; one act flip per film; one ground per world. Sound: A music change on the act flip.
- **Timing:** Changes on cuts and transitions only.
- **Use when:** Any film with more than four shots.
- **Avoid when:** Two neighbouring shots on the same ground with different content.

### Ink resolve on arrival

`cl-ink-resolve` · colour and light · workhorse · energy any · any

Text never simply fades in: it arrives pale (or dim on a dark stage) and darkens or brightens to full ink as it settles.

- **Build:** For each word or line, mix its colour from a pale tone to the ink with mixColor from src/lib/color.ts (interpolateColors stair-steps), while opacity goes from 0.3-0.4 to 1. On paper, go from mixColor(C.ink, C.paper, 0.65), or a pale accent tint mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.8), to C.ink; on a dark stage, go from C.mute to C.white. Pair it with a short rise inside an overflow-hidden line mask (translateY 100% to 0 through arrive(), or at most 60 px), with words staggered and no blur on slow rises; src/fx/Words.tsx can carry the motion while you apply the colour per word. Connector words ('on', 'and', 'the') reach half strength in 2 f and finish over the next 6-12 f, so the nouns read first.
- **Timing:** Colour takes 12-16 f per word on E.out (a headline-scale darkening may run 40 f). The rise takes 20 f, peaking under 20 px/f. Stagger words 8 f apart (4-10). Connector words go 0 to 0.5 in 2 f, then to 1 over 6-12 f.
- **Use when:** Every headline and caption reveal, especially over textured or busy backgrounds where an opacity fade alone looks washed out.
- **Avoid when:** Numbers that must read instantly on a cut (land them at full ink), or type that already sits inside a colour-band fill.

### Key-light edge hairline

`cl-key-light-edge-hairline` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough, sting

Every card, device bezel and bevelled shape on a dark stage carries a hairline edge that is bright on the side facing one fixed key light and fades to nothing on the far side, so surfaces separate from black without shadows or halos.

- **Build:** Declare one light direction for the whole film in brand/tokens.ts (LIGHT = 135, meaning light from the top-left, the same key light cl-tilt-linked-sheen assumes). Give each surface an edge layer above its content: position absolute, inset 0, border-radius inherit, padding 1.5 px, background linear-gradient(calc(LIGHT - rotateZ) deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.40) 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0.10) 35%, transparent 65%), masked to a ring with mask: linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0) and mask-composite: exclude (-webkit-mask-composite: xor). Recompute the angle every frame as LIGHT minus the object's own rotateZ, so the lit edge stays on the light's side while the object turns. Add box-shadow inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06) as a top inner highlight. In 3D, multiply the lit-edge alpha by clamp(1 + 0.04 x degrees tilted toward the light, 0.6, 1.4), so an edge brightens as it turns into the light. For bevelled decorative shapes drawn in SVG (stars, tiles, extruded marks), stroke each facet edge at 1 px with a linearGradient in gradientUnits='userSpaceOnUse' running along the light vector (white at 40% fading to 0), and keep facet fills within 2-4% luma of the stage. Use no blur and no outer halo. On light stages, replace the hairline with a 1.5 px C.white top edge and a C.line bottom edge.
- **Timing:** Static styling with no clock of its own: it rides every entrance and move of its surface. Lit-edge alpha is 0.40 at the light corner, 0.10 at 35% of the gradient line and 0 by 65%. The inner top highlight is 0.06. The angle is recomputed every frame as LIGHT - rotateZ. Tilt gain is 0.04 per degree, clamped to 0.6-1.4x. On a tilt resolve (for example rotateX 25 deg to 0 over 68 f on E.out), the edge brightness settles on the same curve.
- **Use when:** Dark UI films with flat cards, panels, device bezels or bevelled brand shapes on near-black, where a drop shadow disappears and a glow is off-limits.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode shots, where a white hairline vanishes on paper. Also avoid it on cards that already carry cl-rim-light-sweep's travelling streak, and on layouts so dense that every lit edge turns the frame into wireframe noise.

### Monochrome world, one accent

`cl-mono-one-accent` · colour and light · workhorse · energy any · any

Everything is black, white and grey, and one saturated accent marks the single element in each shot that carries the meaning.

- **Build:** Declare neutrals plus one accent in brand/tokens.ts: C.ink for the stage, C.ink2 for surfaces, C.mute for labels, C.line for strokes, C.white for type, C.accent, and a press step of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.08). Grade every photo, map, clay render or backdrop screenshot with filter: grayscale(1) so mixed media reads as one world. Paint the accent on exactly one thing per shot (the payoff word, the pin, the pressed button, the focus ring) and keep one meaning for it all film. Focus devices use three steps of it: the full accent for strokes, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.65) for fills and a mid step for decaying outlines. Colour arrives on a cut or an impact frame (fd(frame) >= cue), never through a slow fade, and when you audit rendered stills the accent should average 0.05-6% of frame pixels (peak about 12.5%) with the stage at 85-90%.
- **Timing:** The palette stays the same for the whole film. The accent swaps on the cue frame (a step, 0 f). Focus outlines land 6-10 px wide with their container (26 f, E.out), thin to 1 px over 12 f on E.in, then decay to 30% opacity over 24 f on E.linear.
- **Use when:** Films that mix photos, 3D, maps and UI, multi-cell layouts, or any shot where several things compete and the eye needs exactly one target.
- **Avoid when:** The product's own colourful UI is the subject of every shot and greying it would misrepresent it, or the story needs two semantic colours on screen at once.

### Now, was, next tone ladder

`cl-read-state-tone-ladder` · colour and light · workhorse · energy any · any

Items in a sequence sit on three neutral tones: the one being read is at full ink, the ones already read step down to a mid grey and stay as context, and the ones still to come wait in a dim grey.

- **Build:** Declare three tones in brand/tokens.ts. NOW is C.white on an ink stage (C.ink on paper). WAS is C.mute. NEXT is mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.24) on ink (mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.2) on paper). Give every item in the sequence (caption words, list rows, step labels, roller slots, status words) a cue frame, and compute its state with fd(): NEXT before its cue, NOW from its cue, and WAS from the next item's cue. Promote NEXT to NOW over 6 f on E.ui. Start the previous item's NOW-to-WAS demotion on the same frame, over 10 f on E.smooth, so the eye is handed over and only one item is at full ink after each handoff. Rollers and ratchets step their tones on the slot frame with no tween. Show pending items at NEXT only when 'there is more' is the message (lists, slot ratchets, step lists, with at most three visible); otherwise they do not exist yet. Exits go through WAS: an item drops to WAS before it leaves, never straight from NOW. Keep weight and size the same so tone alone carries the order. The accent stays out of the ladder because it marks meaning (cl-mono-one-accent).
- **Timing:** Promotion takes 6 f on E.ui. Demotion takes 10 f on E.smooth, starting with the next item's arrival. Each item holds NOW for at least 24 f. Rollers and ratchets step on the slot frame (0 f). An exit starts at least 8 f after the item reaches WAS. On ink, the tones sit at about 100% (NOW), 40% (WAS) and 24% (NEXT) of the way from the stage to white.
- **Use when:** Captions that build in steps, lists and checklists that grow, slot rollers, status sequences, and flanking words that make way for a new focal word.
- **Avoid when:** A single statement that lands all at once, or real product UI whose own text colours must stay true. In lens lists, tone should follow distance from the focus line, not reading order.

### One-hue light ramp

`cl-one-hue-light-ramp` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · launch, sting, feature, loop

Every lit thing (rims, rings, stage lifts, the end-card field) comes from adjacent lightness steps of one hue on a single near-black stage.

- **Build:** Build five tokens of one hue with mixColor, running from the stage to a pale tint: C.ink, then mixColor(C.ink, C.accent, 0.2 / 0.45 / 0.75), then mixColor(C.accent, C.white, 0.5). Only ever draw a gradient between two adjacent steps, so the whole film's light comes from one decision. Rims, rings and orb lobes use the upper steps as crisp strokes or flat fills, never as soft halos or bloom, and the stage holds 63-99% of pixels on dark frames. For an end-card field behind a wordmark, use linear-gradient(to top, step0, step2 45%, step4) plus a repeating-linear-gradient(90deg) of flat, hard-edged 60-120 px bands at ±6% lightness (no blur, so they never read as fluted glass); the band layer drifts 0.3 px/f so the hold never freezes. Against banding, bake the field as a dithered PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py and let the film's global 1.5-2% grain sit over it.
- **Timing:** The palette stays the same. The end-card field holds 90-120 f with the bands drifting 0.3 px/f on E.linear.
- **Use when:** Dark launch films with many light-built shapes (orbs, rings, rims) that need a recognisable look. It also makes a single bright card hit harder.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode walkthroughs where the UI's own colours dominate, or films already using the monochrome-plus-accent system (pick one system).

### Palette shift as context cue

`cl-context-palette-shift` · colour and light · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

The world's colour changes behind a steady foreground, for a whole act or for one beat, to say 'new context' or 'this is the moment' without words.

- **Build:** Keep two or three token sets keyed by act in brand/tokens.ts: for example, a loud act on C.paper with C.ink and C.accent, a technical process act in pure neutral greys, and a calm product act in pale tints of one hue with the accent withdrawn. Read colours through a palette(act) helper so a whole act switches at once, on a hard cut or hidden inside a zoom-through. For a single beat, park the hero (card, composer, device) and shift only the backdrop. Drive one blurred backdrop layer's filter brightness() and saturate() so its luma rises about 100 levels over 42 f on E.smooth, or step it on the cut into the hero beat and step back on the next wide. The hero never moves during the shift, so the eye stays parked.
- **Timing:** Act switches happen in 0 f on a cut. A neutral process act can be as short as 74 f. A backdrop shift takes 42 f on E.smooth. A hero-beat backdrop holds for up to about 300 f before stepping back.
- **Use when:** Act changes without title cards, entering another app's world, or flagging the key moment (the user's prompt, the reveal).
- **Avoid when:** The foreground is moving at the same time (the cue gets lost), or the film is shorter than two acts.

### Soft blobs drift behind the copy

`dv-drifting-blob-field` · colour and light · workhorse · energy calm · any

Large soft colour masses (500-900 px) drift and breathe slowly behind the type, so no ground is flat; a blob can wander continuously and ignore the cuts, or drift and shrink behind a held logo; the colourway can change on cuts.

- **Build:** <LightField pools={[...]}> with Lissajous loops; colourway per shot. Anatomy: 22-37 % of the frame each, about 1 px a frame, area breathing; variant: static soft glows bleeding from the corners with faint layout lines. Sound: None. Materials: A mesh gradient built from two inks: saturated pools of the accent in a pale grey-tinted base with near-white highlights along one S-shaped ribbon; blob blur 25-35 % of the frame width; the shapes drift and bend about 0.5 % a frame and stay continuous across cuts in the same colourway. Two-lobe version: a cool lobe and a warm lobe meeting at a soft vertical seam where their mix shows, the shape morphing from a wedge to an ellipse to a pill over about 2 s spans. Add grain at 1.5-2 % or bake the lobes as dithered plates: large soft gradients band at 8 bits.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Materials:** A mesh gradient built from two inks: saturated pools of the accent in a pale grey-tinted base with near-white highlights along one S-shaped ribbon; blob blur 25-35 % of the frame width; the shapes drift and bend about 0.5 % a frame and stay continuous across cuts in the same colourway. Two-lobe version: a cool lobe and a warm lobe meeting at a soft vertical seam where their mix shows, the shape morphing from a wedge to an ellipse to a pill over about 2 s spans. Add grain at 1.5-2 % or bake the lobes as dithered plates: large soft gradients band at 8 bits.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Continuous; contours repeating every 60 f, bands every 116 f; drift 87 f decelerating.
- **Use when:** Text-led films on a coloured ground.
- **Avoid when:** A second mesh field in other hues; blobs that move faster than about 1 px a frame.

### The interface cast in relief under one key

`cl-key-light-relief` · colour and light · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature

The product's screens and cards stand as shallow blocks on a floor of their own colour, lit by one directional key: every raised thing casts a shadow, sits on a contact shadow and shows lit and shaded faces in one hue, so the film reads as an object in light instead of a flat screen.

- **Build:** Lay the interface out on the floor in px at 1080p and give each element a height by importance (4-40 px; a hero up to 260). Draw it with <ReliefScene blocks camera keyLight floor ink /> under a high three-quarter camera (pitch 50-62, focal about 1.8 x frame height); map each card's HTML onto its top face with `content`. Key from keyLightState: house elevation 34, azimuth 315; one shadow group at 0.18 of ink (up to 0.45 at night on a deep ground) with a fixed 1.5 px penumbra. Taller blocks shade the tops of lower ones automatically. Blur the far rows in a second scene with one fixed blur for depth.
- **Primitive:** `fx/KeyLight.ReliefScene`, `fx/KeyLight.keyLightState`, `fx/KeyLight.reliefState`
- **Timing:** The camera drifts or trucks on every hold (creep); the key moves on its own clock (a rake of 20-40 deg over a shot, or a light event).
- **Use when:** A product with a real interface (cards, lists, a dashboard) and a story about what matters in it.
- **Avoid when:** Photographic product footage carries the film; a relief next to footage reads as two worlds.

### A tint wave travels through the words and drains

`dv-tint-wave-through-words` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A band of tint moves through a line (or a running counter's digits) as the words arrive, peaking on each word as the voice lands it and draining behind; it can park on the last word.

- **Build:** HueSweep on the line with starts on the voice onsets, sweepOn 'all', back on early words; park with Chain accent="hold". Recipe: background linear-gradient(90deg, ink 0 40 %, deep 45 %, accent 50 % 58 %, deep 63 %, ink 68 % 100 %), background-size 300 %, background-clip text, position 100 -> 0 %. Anatomy: Tint band about 1.5 words wide; the picture leads the voice by 1-3 f; drain 12-16 f for early words, the last word lingers; variant: a second, slower wave 30-45 % behind a write-on front; variant: the band parks on the last word. Sound: Voice words land with the tint peaks. Materials: Band shoulders: when the accent travels through type, the band's edges are never a fade to grey. On black type the stops go black -> a deep shade of the accent (about 0.4 letter wide) -> the accent core (1-1.5 letters) -> the deep shade -> black inside single letters; on white type the shoulders are a pale tint instead. Band speed about 1 letter per 4 f on a giant word; in a sentence the head can run about 20 px/f and park on the keyword. Over a counting number the band is a soft-edged tint about 1.5 digits wide crossing in about 50 f while the digits keep running.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`
- **Materials:** Band shoulders: when the accent travels through type, the band's edges are never a fade to grey. On black type the stops go black -> a deep shade of the accent (about 0.4 letter wide) -> the accent core (1-1.5 letters) -> the deep shade -> black inside single letters; on white type the shoulders are a pale tint instead. Band speed about 1 letter per 4 f on a giant word; in a sentence the head can run about 20 px/f and park on the keyword. Over a counting number the band is a soft-edged tint about 1.5 digits wide crossing in about 50 f while the digits keep running.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Word peaks 8 f apart at 60 fps; drain 12-16 f; one pass about 1 s on a counter.
- **Use when:** A headline voiced word by word; a counter that should feel alive; a phrase whose last word is the point.
- **Avoid when:** A grey mid-tone in the band (give it shoulders); a second multi-hue accent in the same film.

### Accent hit envelope

`cl-accent-hit-envelope` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, loop

On a press or an impact, the element floods with the accent and peaks for one frame with its label inverted, then either bleeds back like decaying light or stays as the new state.

- **Build:** Put a solid C.accent overlay inside the button, with the same corner radius. Drive its opacity with hitPulse(frame - cue, 10, 8): a fast rise, a one-frame peak, and an exponential release about twice as long as the attack. Switch the label to C.ink when the overlay passes 0.6, and change no scale (the cursor may dip 1 to 0.9 to 1 over 12 f). For an impact that changes state, swap the object's fill to the accent on the contact frame (decided with fd), add a flat C.white overlay at 0.8·hitPulse(t, 1, 2), apply squash(t) anchored at the contact edge, and leave the accent on. No ring blur and no outer halo.
- **Primitive:** `lib/color.accentFade`
- **Timing:** Attack 10-12 f, a 1 f peak, then a release of 20-26 f (tau 8): an asymmetric 1:2 envelope. On an impact, the swap takes 1 f, the white flash about 4 f and the squash 8 f.
- **Use when:** Primary-button clicks, send or confirm moments, and contact hits that turn an object into its new state.
- **Avoid when:** Secondary controls and hovers (save it for the decisive action), or when the accent already floods the ground.

### Brightness rides the move

`cl-brightness-rides-move` · colour and light · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature

A mark or icon takes its brightness from the same progress that drives its scale or depth, so an oversized pass stays a dark shape and the object reaches full brightness exactly as it lands.

- **Build:** Never give the fill a clock of its own: derive it from the transform. Log-scale slam: s = lmix(s0, 1, prog(f, a, a + 66, E.glide)) with s0 = 6-8. Then p = 1 - Math.log(s) / Math.log(s0), and fill = mixColor(mixColor(C.ink, C.white, 0.14), C.white, p * p * p) on a dark stage (on paper, mix from mixColor(C.paper, C.ink, 0.12) to C.ink). While the mark is three or more times its final size and covering much of the frame, it stays a dark grey under about luma 60, so the frame's mean luma never flashes. Lift toward camera: an icon tile peeling out of its row inverts as it travels, with the tile going mixColor(C.ink2, C.white, q) and the glyph mixColor(C.white, C.ink, q), where q = clamp(travel progress / 0.75), so the inversion finishes before the last quarter of the move. Depth field: in a multi-depth parallax field, mix each layer's fill from C.ink toward its own colour by a weight read from its current z (0.45 far, 0.75 mid, 1.0 near), and keep reading it during a push so objects brighten as they approach. Turn on true motion blur while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and check with scripts/measure-speed.py that edges stay under 80 px/f.
- **Timing:** Slam: 66 f on E.glide from s0 = 6-8. The fill follows p^3, so it passes mid-grey only in the second half of the move and reaches full brightness on the landing frame. Lift-out: 24 f of travel on E.inOut, with the inversion complete at 75% (about 18 f); a mid-grey tile goes from about luma 160 to 248. Depth weights are 0.45 / 0.75 / 1.0 by z, re-read every frame of the push. Motion blur stays on while |delta log s| > 0.1 per frame, and edges stay under 80 px/f.
- **Use when:** A logo mark or icon slams in oversized and shrinks to size, an icon lifts out of the UI toward camera, or a field of objects at several depths is pushed through on a dark stage.
- **Avoid when:** Text (use cl-ink-resolve, which runs on time), and moves under about 150 px or 1.5x, where the change would not show. On a light stage a giant near-black pass would itself be the flash, so mix toward the paper there.

### Category tint crossfades through grey

`dv-tint-through-grey` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

Video panels fade in from white into a duotone with a small saturation overshoot; with each category the tint changes by passing through a neutral grey, so two tints never mix into a third hue.

- **Build:** tintThroughGrey(f, { a, b, grey }) on a Develop duotone. Anatomy: Duotone in; saturation overshoot +52 % then settle; crossfade via grey. Sound: A ding on the first, a sub on the last.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.tintThroughGrey`
- **Timing:** Crossfades 13-18 f each; lines 35 f.
- **Use when:** Several categories or use cases shown on the same panels.
- **Avoid when:** More than about four tints.

### Core glows up to white-hot

`dv-inner-glow-core` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

The core of a hero object brightens to white with a soft halo (or a point's halo blooms wide and contracts, or a held word sits on a faint bloom).

- **Build:** A baked halo plate whose opacity follows haloLevel(); never an animated blur. Anatomy: Core brightness 153 -> 240 in luma with a halo; halo 250 px contracting to 120 px in one step; repeated beats. Sound: A celesta note 53 ms before.
- **Primitive:** `fx/KeyLight`
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 19 f cubic-out, repeated; halo held 5 f then one-step contraction.
- **Use when:** A brand that supplies glow; a living hero object.
- **Avoid when:** House films (a radial glow is the stock look).

### Element enters over-exposed and decays to its tone

`dv-overexposed-entry` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

New figures appear as flat bright white for a few frames and drop to their real tone in one step; a cut-out subject flashes bright on release while the caption slips behind it.

- **Build:** Build: <EntryFlash at color> inside the arriving element (fx/MicroUI): a flat light overlay holds 10 f and drops in one step; mode="decay" fades 1 -> 0 in 5 f (the accent-flash tile on a cut-on). Anatomy: White hold 4 f, one-step drop, near and far figures 2 f apart; variant: +60 L* flash on release, decaying 20 f, with a depth swap of the caption. Sound: A mouse-click on the release. Materials: On the first frame after the white flash, figures arrive as one-frame vertical smears (about 150 px, luminance kept, a 3 px colour split), then sharp flat white silhouettes that decay to grey halftone.
- **Primitive:** `fx/MicroUI.EntryFlash`
- **Materials:** On the first frame after the white flash, figures arrive as one-frame vertical smears (about 150 px, luminance kept, a 3 px colour split), then sharp flat white silhouettes that decay to grey halftone.
- **Timing:** Hold 10 f, drop 1 f; flash hold 5 f, decay 20 f.
- **Use when:** Figures arriving in a graphic world; the release moment of a selection.
- **Avoid when:** Faces that must be read from the first frame.

### Full-frame satin folds of colour that roll through hues

`dv-satin-fold-field` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

Behind small captions the whole frame is a soft field of tall curved folds like satin or an aurora: dark ribbons sweep diagonally through bright bands and the colour phase slowly rolls from one hue through its neighbour into a deep shade; the calm cousin is a field of glossy diagonal stripes over a two-ink gradient that fades to black at the edges.

- **Build:** Recipe: render two fold plates offline as dithered PNGs (scripts/dither-gradient.py) and move and skew them by transform, cross-fading the two phases instead of animating colour. Anatomy: Folds: one colour strip, sin(x * 12 + 0.8 sin(y * 3) + t) through a four-stop ramp, skewed so the folds lean, blurred about 20 px; dark ribbons 80-140 px, highlights about 200 px; phase cycle about 2 s; ripple travel about 3 px/f. Stripes: highlight +12 % luma, 4 px blur, at 135 deg, drifting 1 px/f. Sound: VO or music only. Materials: Ramp: deep shade -> shadow hue -> accent -> highlight tint. Stripes over a radial gradient (120 % x 90 % at the lower left: light tint, accent at 45 %, near-black at 80 %).
- **Primitive:** `fx/Gradients.GradientField`
- **Materials:** Ramp: deep shade -> shadow hue -> accent -> highlight tint. Stripes over a radial gradient (120 % x 90 % at the lower left: light tint, accent at 45 %, near-black at 80 %).
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Continuous, never a held frame.
- **Use when:** A section of short captions over pure colour; music-led films.
- **Avoid when:** Under dense UI; next to another full-frame colour field.

### Ghost pre-flash of an upcoming element

`dv-ghost-preflash` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A huge, faint version of an element that is about to arrive flashes behind the frame for a few frames before the real element lands.

- **Build:** Build: <GhostPreflash land x y>{element}</GhostPreflash> (fx/Flashes): the element at 5.5x, 12 %, for 6 f (creeping 8 % larger), ending 6 f before it lands; a stepped run. Anatomy: Oversized ghost (5-6x) at 8-15 % strength for 5-8 f; the real element lands 3-11 f later. Sound: A whoosh on the flash. Materials: The ghost can be any layer of the coming shot: a full-frame tinted texture at about 35 % for 10 f, a huge faint line etching at about 10 % and twice its final size for 16 f, a silhouette for 2 f, a coloured glow at 20 % screen over the current plate for 20 f. Small marks can do the same job: corner marks switch to the next shot's accent 4-8 f before the cut, one corner a frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flashes.GhostPreflash`
- **Materials:** The ghost can be any layer of the coming shot: a full-frame tinted texture at about 35 % for 10 f, a huge faint line etching at about 10 % and twice its final size for 16 f, a silhouette for 2 f, a coloured glow at 20 % screen over the current plate for 20 f. Small marks can do the same job: corner marks switch to the next shot's accent 4-8 f before the cut, one corner a frame.
- **Timing:** Ghost 5-8 f; real element +3-11 f.
- **Use when:** A collage or stop-motion build that should anticipate its next piece.
- **Avoid when:** Clean UI films.

### Graphic softens into the stage

`cl-graphic-blurs-into-stage` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, loop

A crisp graphic that has just finished its move, such as a wall of bars or a stripe field, loses its edges, widens and keeps drifting until it has become the soft backdrop for the next title, with no cut.

- **Build:** Keep the graphic's own elements mounted after their build and render them through src/fx/RackFocus (render = the bar group, blur 48, mid on). Drive t from 0 to 1 over 72 f on E.smooth. RackFocus crossfades a sharp copy and a copy at constant blur, so the softening does not step the way an animated filter: blur() does. On the same progress, widen each element (scaleX 1 to 1.5 about its centre) so the gaps close, and mix the whole field 25% toward the stage colour so its contrast drops under the type to come. Fill every element with a vertical gradient between two adjacent steps of the film's one-hue ramp (cl-one-hue-light-ramp). Slide each element's background-position-y at its own speed, 0.3 + 0.5 x rand(i) percent per frame, so the bands shift tone at different rates and the field never freezes once it is soft. Bring the next foreground in from frame 36 of the soften, when the stripes no longer read as objects. If banding shows, add 1-2% feTurbulence noise over the field, or bake a matching still with scripts/dither-gradient.py. In full colour, the field shifts through several hues as it softens.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Fill the bars with tonal steps of one non-banned hue (from the stage to a light tint), not a periwinkle-pink-orange spectrum, so the softened field becomes a single-hue living stage. Keep the RackFocus soften, the widen and the per-bar drift. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The soften takes 72 f on E.smooth (RackFocus t from 0 to 1, blur 48 px at 1080p). The widen from 1 to 1.5 and the 25% contrast drop run on the same curve. Each element's gradient drifts at 0.3-0.8% per frame on E.linear and keeps drifting for 60-120 f under the next element. The next foreground enters from frame 36.
- **Use when:** After a graphic build (a bar wall, a stripe or tile field, a filled pattern), when the next beat is a title or the end-card mark and needs a backdrop born from what was just on screen.
- **Avoid when:** The graphic carries data the viewer still needs to read, or it is a UI act where the stage should stay flat. When no graphic build comes before the title, use cl-living-stage directly.

### Ground darkens or drains as an exit

`dv-ground-drain` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · any

The white page darkens to black with luma halving per frame while its elements shrink out; a panel drains to grey and darkens slowly; the ground dims to true black under an opening.

- **Build:** Recipe: ground colour tween on E.buildIn; shrink the elements with exits 'launch' on scale. Anatomy: Accelerating darken (ease-in), chips shrinking one by one; drain S-curve then linear darken. Sound: A snare starting it. Materials: Grades as a transition: before a chapter cut the whole frame drains (saturation about 60 -> 15 %, brightness to 0.75) over 16 f ease-in, then a hard cut lands on the brightest frame of the film, so the cut reads as a flash without a white frame. When a white page darkens (luma halving each frame), white pills that were invisible on it suddenly read as raised capsules for a beat before they shrink away.
- **Materials:** Grades as a transition: before a chapter cut the whole frame drains (saturation about 60 -> 15 %, brightness to 0.75) over 16 f ease-in, then a hard cut lands on the brightest frame of the film, so the cut reads as a flash without a white frame. When a white page darkens (luma halving each frame), white pills that were invisible on it suddenly read as raised capsules for a beat before they shrink away.
- **Timing:** 25-40 f; drain 33 f then 128 f.
- **Use when:** The end of a section; an opening that builds on black.
- **Avoid when:** A plain fade to black between unrelated shots.

### Ground flips on one frame as punctuation

`dv-ground-flip-on-beat` · colour and light · accent · energy high · any

The background inverts (dark to light) on one frame while the objects stay; or a whole background layer switches from dim grey to the accent on the key word; or a colour change passes through a one-frame near-black dip on a pop.

- **Build:** HardStep on the ground colour; the dip as a one-frame fill. Anatomy: One-frame switch; optional one-frame dip; objects unchanged. Sound: The resolving word or a pop 33 ms after. Materials: Ground and type swap colours through one half-blend frame: the type turns 50 % for a single frame, then the whole palette has swapped (accent type on white instead of white on accent) while small labels keep their colour.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HardStep`
- **Materials:** Ground and type swap colours through one half-blend frame: the type turns 50 % for a single frame, then the whole palette has swapped (accent type on white instead of white on accent) while small labels keep their colour.
- **Timing:** 1-2 f; a dip variant 12 f to the dip, 10 f back.
- **Use when:** The key word of a line; a beat inside a held shot.
- **Avoid when:** More than one or two per film (polarity flips are the loudest punctuation).

### Ground gradient swaps or floods

`dv-gradient-ground-swap` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch

Behind a locked picture the two stops of a vertical gradient trade places; or a brand gradient floods half the frame behind stripes.

- **Build:** Baked dithered gradient plates cross-faded by opacity. Bake every gradient with scripts/dither-gradient.py from one stop list in the brand tokens. Anatomy: Stops swap over 48 f; flood coverage 0.14 -> 0.96 in 100 f. Sound: A reverse-cymbal swell. Materials: One gradient family everywhere: every gradient in the film (strips, light floods, skies, mesh grounds) uses the same five stops, ordered by lightness so no muddy midpoint appears (e.g. a warm stop always sits between the hot hue and white, never beside the cool one); large soft gradients carry a fine per-pixel dither (sigma about 0.75 levels) that only shows under a contrast boost. Variants: a diagonal three-hue ground under floating panels; a pale sky radial (near-white centre, pale blue corners) with blurred clouds drifting about 0.5 px/f that hides every UI scene in air.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Materials:** One gradient family everywhere: every gradient in the film (strips, light floods, skies, mesh grounds) uses the same five stops, ordered by lightness so no muddy midpoint appears (e.g. a warm stop always sits between the hot hue and white, never beside the cool one); large soft gradients carry a fine per-pixel dither (sigma about 0.75 levels) that only shows under a contrast boost. Variants: a diagonal three-hue ground under floating panels; a pale sky radial (near-white centre, pale blue corners) with blurred clouds drifting about 0.5 px/f that hides every UI scene in air.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** 48-100 f.
- **Use when:** Any film that carries one gradient family.
- **Avoid when:** House films.

### Hard colour swaps that step the size

`dv-hard-fill-swaps` · colour and light · accent · energy high · launch, feature, sting

A shape (a pair of circles, discs, a column) hard-cuts through three fills a few frames apart, each swap also stepping it about 4 % larger; or a column switches colour on the frame it passes half its width.

- **Build:** fillSwapState(f, { at, n: 3, every: 10, grow: 0.04, fills }). Anatomy: 3 swaps, each with a scale step x1.04; text dims a frame before; variant: a column widens 6x and swaps colour at half width with a band of the old colour inside. Sound: Swaps next to a kick and a sub-drop. Materials: The pair cuts through three fills, each held exactly 10 f and each slightly larger (+4 % a step), on third-beats; the text colour switches on the same frame as the fill, and the words can first sink into the disc colour over 6 f before the first swap.
- **Primitive:** `fx/CutFx.fillSwapState`
- **Materials:** The pair cuts through three fills, each held exactly 10 f and each slightly larger (+4 % a step), on third-beats; the text colour switches on the same frame as the fill, and the words can first sink into the disc colour over 6 f before the first swap.
- **Timing:** Swaps 10 f apart at 60 fps (6 Hz); widen 20 f cubic-out.
- **Use when:** A beat-cut on a simple graphic; building energy before a reveal.
- **Avoid when:** More than one run per act.

### Heat ramp as the arrival and exit colour system

`dv-heat-ramp-arrive-exit` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

Every arrival cools from a warm tint to the ink and every exit heats back up and bleaches to white; colour leads the fade, so type seems to burn in and burn out.

- **Build:** HueSweep with back for exits (one hue path, lightness doing the work). Anatomy: Arrival: pale warm -> accent -> deep -> ink; exit: ink -> warm -> pale -> white, colour leading opacity. Sound: None of its own.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** One hue: pale accent -> accent -> ink on arrival, the reverse plus a fade on exit. The full look relies on orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Cool 10-15 f; heat 8-23 f.
- **Use when:** A whole film's colour grammar, one film at a time.
- **Avoid when:** Brands without a warm accent; mixing with other accent systems.

### Light bands flow along a column

`dv-gradient-band-flow` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Bands of a lighter tint sweep down a coloured column at constant speed, new pulses every 25 f: the column reads as a channel with something flowing.

- **Build:** <LightField bands={[{ plate, width, y, period, dir: 'down' }]}>. Anatomy: Leading edge at a constant 256 px/f; pulses every 25 f. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Timing:** Constant speed; continuous.
- **Use when:** A pipe, a column, a stream of data.
- **Avoid when:** Beat-locking it (it should run free).

### Light cone drops and flashes twice

`dv-light-cone-drop` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

An inverted-triangle beam drops from the top edge, widening, and flashes colour twice on UI pops.

- **Build:** LightField glowRise on a static cone plate scaled by transform; flashes as opacity steps. Anatomy: Width 487 -> 1447 px circ-out; two colour flashes 0.25 s apart. Sound: The second flash 34 ms after a UI pop.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Timing:** 38 f; flashes at about 15 f and 30 f.
- **Use when:** A spotlight on a hero object.
- **Avoid when:** Saturated beams.

### Light sweep across a landing

`tr-light-sweep` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, loop

A soft band of light swings across the frame as a product lands, accelerating like a beam passing the lens: a light event without a glow on any element.

- **Build:** <LightSweep frame start frames band angle gain />, screen blend, one hue (white or a pale accent tint), on a dark stage.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure.LightSweep`
- **Timing:** 44 f on E.launchIn across the frame plus the band, band 0.45 of the width, gain 0.2-0.55.
- **Use when:** A product or card lands on an ink stage and the act needs its light event.
- **Avoid when:** Paper grounds (a white band on paper is invisible; use an exposure or a light field).

### Living light under every hold

`cl-living-stage` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, update, feature, loop, vertical

A one-hue light field under the scene that rises into each reveal on the beat (a floor glow climbing on the hit); between reveals it holds still, never pools wandering to keep a still frame busy.

- **Build:** Bake the plates with scripts/dither-gradient.py (kinds floor, pool, loop; give each the ground with "over" and run --check). <LightField frame floor={{ plate, height, strength, breathe, lift }} pools={[...]} bands={[...]} glowRise={{ at, gain: 2, dur }} /> under the scene. Lightness swing 0.05-0.20 at chroma 0.13 or less, accent hue only. Never animate a CSS gradient.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField.LightField`, `fx/LightField.lightFieldState`
- **Timing:** Pools 240 px/s at 1080p on 1-4 s loops; a band one tile every 2 s; a rise x2 over 0.9 s peaking on the hit.
- **Use when:** Calm text holds over a coloured or mid ground where a reveal wants light on its beat.
- **Avoid when:** A key-lit relief already gives the hold its light change (use one light system per shot).

### Object materialises through a colour wash

`dv-colour-wash-materialise` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A board or object starts as a flat colour overlay and sweeps through tints before landing on its true colours; or an object is recoloured through a gradient map for 5 frames on a hit.

- **Build:** <Develop> (duotone tint -> full colour) for the wash; a one-hue flash as a HardStep overlay on the object. Anatomy: Overlay colour -> tints -> true colours; gradient-map flash on an object within 22 f. Sound: A hit on the flash.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Develop`
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Wash 54 f; flash 10 f inside 22 f.
- **Use when:** The first appearance of a product board; a hit on a dock or icon row.
- **Avoid when:** A second multi-hue wash in the same film.

### Previous hero knocked back in one frame

`dv-one-frame-knockback` · colour and light · accent · energy high · launch, feature

When the big type arrives, the previous hero drops to about 55 % strength in a single frame, so the eye moves to the new element.

- **Build:** Build: knockback(f, land) (fx/Flashes): the previous hero's strength drops to 55 % on the new hero's landing frame (one stepped frame). Anatomy: One-frame opacity step to 0.55. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Flashes.knockback`
- **Timing:** 1 f.
- **Use when:** Stacking a new statement over a previous visual.
- **Avoid when:** Fading it slowly (that reads as indecision).

### Rising colour wash carrier

`cl-rising-wash-carrier` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

A soft single-hue field rises from the bottom edge behind the type, swells and sweeps up across the frame on the change, then recedes off the top, so the foreground swap reads as one move.

- **Build:** Place a full-frame layer under the type with background radial-gradient(ellipse 70% 60% at 50% Y, C.accent 0%, transparent 70%). The gradient is soft on its own, so use no blur filter, keep normal blend and keep the saturation low. Animate Y from 110% to 75% on E.out (coverage 0 to 47%). Then swell the ellipse from 70% to 110% and wipe it up (centroid from about 487 to 154 px at 1080p) on E.inOut, changing the foreground underneath on the fastest frame, and finally let it recede to Y -20% on E.outSoft. Short version into a hard cut: a bottom-anchored band of 40% height, linear-gradient(to top, mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.5), transparent), translateY from 100% to 20% on E.in, with the cut landing mid-rise. Use it to preview the accent ground that is coming.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the move and lose the soft falloff: a flat accent band with a crisp, straight top edge (a clip-path inset driven by the same Y curve) rises behind the type, sweeps up across the frame on the change and leaves off the top, at full opacity in a light tint of the accent. The swap still happens on its fastest frame; no radial gradient, no feathered edge. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** The rise takes 39 f on E.out. The swell and wipe take 12 f on E.inOut (about 28 px/f). The recede takes 90 f on E.outSoft. The pre-cut band takes 16 f on E.in (about +14 luma levels).
- **Use when:** Changing cards behind continuous colour, leading into an accent-ground claim or the end card, or smoothing a hard cut into a new scene.
- **Avoid when:** Shots already on an accent ground, or dense UI that the wash would tint. A soft accent haze behind type reads as glow.

### Shadows tinted by the stage

`cl-hue-tinted-shadow` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch

On a tinted light stage, lifted cards and solid pills cast soft shadows in a dark step of the stage's own hue instead of grey, so depth reads as part of the world's colour rather than dirt on it.

- **Build:** Derive one shadow colour from the stage, never from the accent: SH = mixColor(stageHue, C.ink, 0.6), where stageHue is the act's tint (for example, the pale-tint act of cl-context-palette-shift). Give each lifted card two shadows: a contact shadow, 0 2px 6px of C.ink at 0.10, and an ambient shadow, 0 24px 56px -16px of SH at 0.22 (convert mixColor's rgb() output to rgba). Under a solid black pill or icon tile, use a single tinted ellipse instead. Make it 80% of the element's width and 30% of its height, offset downward by 40% of its height, filled with radial-gradient(SH at 0.35, transparent 70%) and blur(32px), on multiply, below the element. Tie the shadow to lift: with lift = scale - 1 (or translateZ / 200), multiply offset and blur by 1 + 3 x lift and alpha by 1 / (1 + 3 x lift), so a rising card's shadow spreads and fades. Because SH reads from the act's tokens, a palette switch retints every shadow on the same frame. In its richer form, the look puts blurred blobs of two pastel hues beside a black pill and coloured halos on three sides of cards floating on black.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Use only one dark step of the stage's own hue, on light stages only, with shadows that fall downward and never spread past about half the element's size. On dark stages, drop the tint entirely and separate cards with cl-key-light-edge-hairline instead of a coloured halo. The full look relies on glow, gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Static while parked. On a lift (scale 1 to 1.04 over 20-26 f on E.out), the ambient blur goes from about 56 to 63 px and the alpha from 0.22 to 0.20 on the same curve. On seating, it returns on the seat move's own easing. A palette switch retints the shadows in 0 f, on the cut.
- **Use when:** Light-mode acts on pale tinted stages, pastel product worlds, and black pills or tiles floating on a tinted field where a grey shadow looks muddy.
- **Avoid when:** Dark stages, where a coloured shadow becomes a glow. Keep shadows neutral in neutral C.paper films, and skip the tint wherever it would echo the accent and spend its meaning.

### Small token cycles through hues

`dv-hue-cycle-token` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A version number or a pill border keeps cycling through hues (or a rotating multi-colour stroke) while the wordmark stays ink.

- **Build:** Brand path colour cycle; the border as a conic gradient (a baked plate) rotated by transform. Anatomy: Hue stops 22-26 f each; a border gradient rotating about 6 deg a frame. Sound: None.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** The token breathes in lightness at the accent hue (a 0.05-0.10 L swing over 1-2 s). The full look relies on purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Stops 22-26 f; continuous.
- **Use when:** A version tag or an "active" pill in a brand with a multi-colour system.
- **Avoid when:** House films (it reads as a template).

### Soft light hops to the active card

`dv-focus-glow-hop` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A soft light appears behind one card or tile and moves to the next as each becomes active; a dark grid of keycap tiles lights up tile by tile as labels fade in.

- **Build:** LightField pool moved between card centres on E.snapOut. Anatomy: Soft light about 100 px around the active element; moves card to card; grows about 2.5x on the tile variant. Sound: None, or a soft tick per hop. Materials: The light is motivated: a small passing foreground dot leaves a soft radial glow on each card it crosses (a pale accent tint at about 0.55 at the core, radius about 70 px), blooming 2 f after the dot passes and fading over 20 f, so the glow seems lit by the dot.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Materials:** The light is motivated: a small passing foreground dot leaves a soft radial glow on each card it crosses (a pale accent tint at about 0.55 at the core, radius about 70 px), blooming 2 f after the dot passes and fading over 20 f, so the glow seems lit by the dot.
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 28 f per hop; tile bloom 14 f.
- **Use when:** Walking through KPI cards or a grid of features.
- **Avoid when:** Glow halos on light grounds.

### The cut frame glows and decays

`dv-cut-glow-decay` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

On the cut frame the whole stage lifts into a soft glow centred on the subject and decays by a constant ratio over half a second; a dark scene can open over-bloomed and let its halo fall.

- **Build:** <Exposure> with up 0, peak on the cut and down 30 on an exponential. Anatomy: Peak on one frame, decay x0.92 a frame toward the base; halo falls about 70 %. Sound: A whoosh into the cut, or an orchestral stab on the beat.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure`
- **Timing:** Peak 1 f, decay 30-39 f.
- **Use when:** A cut onto a small bright subject on a dark stage.
- **Avoid when:** Light stages (it reads as a flash fault).

### Tiles warm up, then bleach to white

`dv-tint-pulse-bleach` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

All tiles on a wall warm from grey through a tint over a few frames, then bleach to pure white: a colour pulse that carries a transition.

- **Build:** <Exposure> with hue = a pale tint of the accent and swap at the peak. Anatomy: Grey -> tint -> pale -> white; whole wall at once. Sound: A sub on the bleach.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Pulse through a tint of the accent, then bleach. The full look relies on orange; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Exposure`
- **Timing:** Warm 18 f, bleach 20 f.
- **Use when:** Leaving a grid of images into a white scene.
- **Avoid when:** Warm hues in a cool brand.

### Tilt-linked sheen

`cl-tilt-linked-sheen` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, sting

As a card or device tilts in 3D, a faint highlight band slides across its face in step with the angle, so the surface reads as a real material catching a key light.

- **Build:** Inside the tilted element, add an overlay above the content and below its 1 px border: linear-gradient(105deg, transparent 40%, C.white at 18% alpha 50%, transparent 60%) at background-size 300%, with screen blend on dark UI or soft-light on light UI. Compute background-position-x from the same rotation value that drives the transform (50% plus 2.5% per degree of rotateY, with rotateX nudging it vertically), so the highlight moves only while the object turns and parks when it settles. Multiply its opacity by clamp((|rotateY| - 2) / 6) so a flat card stays clean. Assume one key light 45° camera-left for the whole film, so every card catches it from the same side.
- **Timing:** It follows the tilt move: for example, rotateY going from 12° to 0 over 40 f on E.out moves the band about 30% and parks it. Peak overlay opacity is 0.18 on dark UI and 0.10 on light UI.
- **Use when:** Perspective UI tilt-ups, cards flipping or settling out of 3D, device turns, and logo tiles yawing.
- **Avoid when:** Flat 2D layouts with no rotation (use the one-shot specular sweep instead).

### Travelling tone band fill

`cl-tone-band-fill` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, sting, feature

A word, URL or logo mark fills through a band of colour (dark, then accent, then light) that sweeps across it and settles on the final ink.

- **Build:** Text: set background to linear-gradient(90deg, final ink 0 35%, light accent tint 50%, C.accent 65%, stage colour 80%) at background-size 300%, with background-clip: text and color: transparent, and animate background-position from 100% to 0%. For a domain plus path, delay the path span. For accent words in a tagline, step each letter from ink to C.accent with a 2 f stagger after the line lands. Mark: use the mark as an SVG mask over a tall gradient rect, reveal the fill bottom-up with clip-path from inset(100% 0 0 0) to inset(0), then translateY the rect by one gradient period so the tone scrolls and settles on solid accent, just before the colour floods the frame. The type itself stays still; only the fill travels.
- **Timing:** A word sweep takes 32 f on E.smooth (the front peaks at about 25 px/f). A URL takes 42 f, easing into the final ink on E.out, with the path lagging 8-12 f. A mark wipe takes 8 f on E.linear, then the tone scrolls for 36 f on E.smooth. Letters stagger 2 f.
- **Use when:** Hero words, the URL card, or a logo mark that should introduce the accent before it fills the frame.
- **Avoid when:** Small UI text, or type that is still moving (the band and the motion fight).

### Type changes colour with what is behind it

`dv-type-knockout-over-colour` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A soft blob slides under a typed word and the letters over it knock out to white; big type takes its colour from a blurred image blooming behind it; a small caption flips colour the frame a picture passes under it.

- **Build:** Recipe: render the text twice and clip the white copy with the blob's (static, transformed) mask; or mix-blend-mode difference on a flat field. Anatomy: Two copies of the type (ink and knockout), the knockout clipped by the blob or image shape. Sound: None. Materials: A defocused, heavily grained iridescent image (teal, magenta, coral on periwinkle) blooms up from a corner behind the giant type (coverage 7 -> 80 % in 32 f) and splits the letters white or black in screen space: white where the bloom covers the paper, black elsewhere, with a mask feather of about 150 px and grain sigma about 1.5.
- **Materials:** A defocused, heavily grained iridescent image (teal, magenta, coral on periwinkle) blooms up from a corner behind the giant type (coverage 7 -> 80 % in 32 f) and splits the letters white or black in screen space: white where the bloom covers the paper, black elsewhere, with a mask feather of about 150 px and grain sigma about 1.5.
- **Timing:** Blob 22 f expo-out; bloom 33 f; flips on one frame.
- **Use when:** Type that shares the frame with moving colour.
- **Avoid when:** Low contrast in the mixed state.

### Type filled with a gradient that blooms

`dv-gradient-fill-type` · colour and light · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A key phrase grows a little and its fill turns from white into a soft gradient that blooms, or each word of a hero line carries its own soft gradient and lands in silence.

- **Build:** HueSweep with a brand path, or the phrase clipped to a baked dithered gradient plate revealed by opacity. Recipe: a glow copy (blur 20 px, opacity 0.5) under a fill copy clipped to a baked dithered gradient plate; scale on the wrapper. Anatomy: Fill shift white -> gradient over the scale-up (25-30 %), soft bloom; per-word gradients on paper. Sound: The music stops for about 1 s under it. Materials: Construction: the phrase grows 25-30 % over about 58 f while its fill shifts in the first 24 f from white to a horizontal two-hue gradient (a lilac-like left to a sky-like right), with a glow made of a duplicate blurred 18-24 px at about 50 % in a deeper hue behind it; the second word held slightly out of focus (4-6 px). Behind a card, big type can carry a gradient that fades from the saturated hue to nearly the ground colour across the word, so the card in front reads first and the phrase reads as an echo.
- **Primitive:** `fx/HueSweep`
- **Materials:** Construction: the phrase grows 25-30 % over about 58 f while its fill shifts in the first 24 f from white to a horizontal two-hue gradient (a lilac-like left to a sky-like right), with a glow made of a duplicate blurred 18-24 px at about 50 % in a deeper hue behind it; the second word held slightly out of focus (4-6 px). Behind a card, big type can carry a gradient that fades from the saturated hue to nearly the ground colour across the word, so the card in front reads first and the phrase reads as an echo.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform; light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** 42-68 f expo-out.
- **Use when:** A brand that owns a gradient; a hero line once.
- **Avoid when:** More than one gradient phrase per film; a gradient that is not the film's own family.

### Type solidity arc

`cl-type-solidity-arc` · colour and light · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

The type gains body across the film. Early statements are translucent white that lets the coloured stage show through, and the closing line and lockup are solid, so the payoff reads as more certain than the promise.

- **Build:** Add a typeAlpha value to each act in timeline.ts, for example [0.65, 0.85, 1.0] for opening, middle and end, and read it through one helper so every caption in an act shares it. Apply it as the opacity of the C.white line container, not as per-glyph rgba, which darkens where glyphs overlap, so the stage colour shows through the letters. Keep weight, size and tracking identical across acts so that only confidence changes. Step the value only on cuts or act changes, never inside a line or a shot. cl-ink-resolve still handles each arrival; the arc only sets where that resolve ends. Keep translucent acts to display type (at least 64 px at 1080p) over stage areas darker than about luma 110, and check contrast on rendered stills (Stills.tsx). The end-card line and lockup are always solid C.white.
- **Timing:** Act values are 0.65, 0.85 and 1.0 (opening, middle, end), stepped in 0 f on cuts or act changes. Each arrival's ink resolve (12-16 f on E.out) lands at the act's value. The end-card line and lockup stay at 1.0 for their whole 90-120 f hold.
- **Use when:** Brand films and launches on a coloured or living stage, built as question to answer or promise to proof, where the closing line should feel firmer than the opening.
- **Avoid when:** Neutral black or grey stages, where translucent white just reads as dim grey. Also avoid it for small UI text, in films under about 10 s, and on light stages, where translucent ink loses contrast.

### Accent ground for claims only

`cl-accent-claim-grounds` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting, vertical

Narrative shots sit on the neutral stage, other claims flip to the opposite neutral, and the single full-bleed accent ground is saved for the hero claim or the closing card, so colour works as punctuation.

- **Build:** Use two ground tokens (C.paper or C.ink, and C.accent) and one ink. Tag each shot 'story' or 'claim' in timeline.ts. The accent floods the frame once per film: give the full-bleed accent ground to the one hero claim (about 72 f) or to the closing card, and set every other claim on the opposite neutral stage (C.ink after C.paper, or the reverse) with the accent only on its one key word, so accent pixels stay near 8% across the film. Switch grounds on hard cuts; elsewhere the accent appears only as a one-word highlight or a soft single-hue wash that previews the flood. Let the accent ground arrive as a radial flood. Layer order: the accent ground; a disc of radius 640 px whose fill steps mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.75), then 0.4, then 0; a 60 px ring of mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.1) at r 600 px, which appears with the last step and stays for the shot to frame the hero word; then the type.
- **Timing:** Grounds swap on cut frames. The radial flood takes 6 f, with tint steps on f0, f2 and f4 decided with fd(). The ring stays from f4 to the end of the shot. Claim shots run 60-120 f each.
- **Use when:** Films with a few big statements that must feel louder than the walkthrough around them, and endings that need to feel conclusive.
- **Avoid when:** The accent fails contrast as a ground for display type, or the film has no distinct claims (a pure UI tour).

### Cards flood with colour and defocus one by one

`dv-flood-defocus-cards` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

On the line "more than anyone can track", each card turns fully into the brand colour and blurs into a soft blob in a few frames, staggered around the ring, then the whole frame fades to white.

- **Build:** Recipe: Cards with an overlay of the accent (opacity tween) and RackFocus levels per card; Exposure to white at the end. Anatomy: Per card a colour flood overlay plus a fixed defocus ladder; clockwise stagger; white fade. Sound: Voice cadence.
- **Timing:** Flood 8 f, fade 10 f, stagger 5-6 f.
- **Use when:** Showing overload: too many tools, tabs, tasks.
- **Avoid when:** Light brand colours (the blobs disappear).

### False-colour palette cycles, then resolves material by material

`dv-thermal-lut-cycle` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A 3D room is shown in a thermal false-colour palette whose hues rotate while the camera pushes in, then each material resolves to its real look in turn (desk, wall, ceiling).

- **Build:** Recipe: a grey plate through a static colour-map filter whose hue is rotated per frame, per-material masks fading to the true plate. Anatomy: Hue rotation on a luminance map; resolve per material mask. Sound: A riser into it, then quiet. Materials: A blurred backdrop photo (12 px) inside an iris is gradient-mapped to saturated pastels with a map whose hue keeps rolling (about 6 f per stop through six stops) under a thin white cell grid (1 px at 35 %, 12 px pitch), while the whole layer fades out over 36 f.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Cycle a two-tone map of the accent's lightness steps, then resolve. The full look relies on orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/GradientMap.GradientMap`
- **Materials:** A blurred backdrop photo (12 px) inside an iris is gradient-mapped to saturated pastels with a map whose hue keeps rolling (about 6 f per stop through six stops) under a thin white cell grid (1 px at 35 %, 12 px pitch), while the whole layer fades out over 36 f.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Cycle 77 f; resolves 12-20 f each inside a 53 f window.
- **Use when:** A film about sensing, rendering or AI vision.
- **Avoid when:** Without a real 3D or photo plate to map.

### Light swell bridge into the hero

`cl-light-swell-bridge` · colour and light · signature · energy high · launch, sting

Light swells around a small panel until the frame is bright, the film cuts on the brightest frame to the hero card sitting in the same light, and that light slowly exhales back to dark.

- **Build:** Shot A: a radial gradient centred on the panel with four stops (stage, dark tint, mid, light tint), whose radii grow at 12-25 px/f on E.linear so mean frame luma climbs about 2.25 levels per frame (from 15 to about 78); cut on a downbeat at the peak. Shot B opens on the identical gradient with the hero title already in place, then pulls the stops back inward so luma falls from about 112 to 43, handing off to the next dark shot. Put the cut on an act boundary so it stays crisp.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the soft multi-hue bloom with four hard-edged concentric discs in tonal steps of one hue (the stage, then 15%, 35% and 60% lightness toward the accent), their radii expanding with a 2 f stagger on normal blend. Keep the same swell, cut and exhale timing. The full look relies on glow, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField.LightField`, `fx/Exposure.Exposure`
- **Timing:** The swell takes 28 f on E.linear. Cut at the peak, on a downbeat. The exhale takes 86 f on E.smooth (a fade-out never runs on an expo-out).
- **Use when:** Releasing a dark section into the hero card or title: the biggest reveal in a dark film.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode films, or a second time in the same film.

### Noon lift: the light climbs and one thing keeps its shadow

`cl-noon-lift` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A raking key climbs from 8 to 72 degrees in about 1.2 s: every long shadow collapses and the world brightens, while the one element the product surfaces keeps rising and keeps the only long shadow.

- **Build:** In a relief (cl-key-light-relief) add the event { kind: 'noon', at, from: 8, to: 72 } (house 1.2 s on E.strongInOut). Ten frames after it starts, raise the surfaced block's height 18 -> 260 px over about 1.2 s on E.glideOut and give its top face the accent. Push the camera toward it on the same beat. Print the line about it raised on the floor in front of it so its shadow shrinks too.
- **Primitive:** `fx/KeyLight.keyLightState`, `fx/KeyLight.ReliefScene`
- **Timing:** Lift 72 f; rise 70-75 f starting 10 f in; shadows: a 20 px card goes from 142 px to 6 px, the 260 px block keeps 84 px.
- **Use when:** The film's point is that one thing matters among many (the alert, the free hour, the anomaly).
- **Avoid when:** Nothing in the world is raised: the lift then only brightens a flat ground.

### People become flat colour silhouettes

`dv-segmentation-silhouette` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

The people in a collage of tiles switch to flat colour silhouettes with a scattered stagger, then the backgrounds go flat too: a segmentation look that says "the AI sees them".

- **Build:** Recipe: Cutouts mattes (hand-traced polygons) filled flat, switched on per tile with a seeded stagger. Anatomy: Per tile a matte layer in one flat colour; staggered over 4 f; backgrounds follow. Sound: None, or a soft scan.
- **Timing:** 23 f ease-in.
- **Use when:** A film about vision, detection or editing.
- **Avoid when:** Without hand-made mattes (it needs clean cut-outs).

### Rolling band flood

`cl-rolling-band-flood` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A light frame fills with the brand colour as soft horizontal bands of it roll upward and grow opaque. The text tints and dissolves into it, and the film arrives on its end-card field without a cut.

- **Build:** Over the last product frame, add a full-frame overlay holding a strip three frames tall: a linear-gradient(to bottom) that repeats six soft tonal bands of one hue (mixColor(C.accent, C.paper, 0.7), then 0.45, then 0.2, then C.accent, then back up). Make each band about half the frame height, with its stops blending over about 10% of the band. Drive the strip's translateY from 0 to -1 frame height on E.linear, so the bands roll up at constant speed. Drive its opacity with p * p, where p = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.linear), so the colour arrives late and decisively (quarter strength at the halfway point). Mix the foreground text to mixColor(C.accent, C.ink, 0.4) over the first 12 f, then fade it from 1 to 0 over f12-f40 on E.smooth, so the colour absorbs it rather than covering it. End on the end-card field, with the same bands slowing to a 0.3 px/f drift, and let the lockup appear on it afterwards. Bake the strip once with scripts/dither-gradient.py (space oklab) so the soft bands do not contour. In full colour, the flood runs through several hues.
