- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Build the bands only from tonal steps of one non-banned hue (light tint, mid tint, the accent), not a lavender-pink-peach-orange spectrum. Keep the roll, the p^2 opacity ramp and the text absorption. The full look relies on gradient, orange, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 60 f in total. The bands roll one frame height on E.linear (about 18 px/f at 1080p), and the opacity follows p^2 over the same 60 f. The text tints over 12 f and fades over f12-f40 on E.smooth. Frame mean luma goes from about 250 to 215: a light-to-mid flood, not a polarity flip. The bands then ease to a 0.3 px/f drift for the end card's 90-120 f.
- **Use when:** Closing a light product act into the end card, or returning to the brand world after the last UI beat (a success state, a published page) without a hard cut.
- **Avoid when:** Dark films, where the flood reads as fog over black. Also avoid it a second time in the same film, and before an end card whose ground is not the flood's hue.

### Single inversion card

`cl-inversion-card` · colour and light · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

In an otherwise dark film, one card cuts to a near-white field with dark type for one second, marking the key promise.

- **Build:** At about 40% of runtime, inside a gap in the music, hard-cut to an AbsoluteFill of cream C.paper whose edges carry a soft ring of colour, fading from white at 55% of the radius through two accent hues to the frame edge. Set the line in C.ink and rise it out of a line mask: overflow hidden, translateY from 100% to 0 through arrive(), on E.out. Let the ring breathe, with its scale moving between 1.00 and 1.02 on sin(2π·frame/120). Frame mean luma jumps from about 9 to about 232, so this must be the film's only light frame; cut out hard on the next beat.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep a neutral C.paper field, never a cream one. Draw the ring as a single hard-edged accent stroke (a 6-10 px ellipse at 88% of the frame) that breathes in scale, with no soft colour falloff and no second hue. The full look relies on gradient, beige; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Hold for 60 f. The type rises over 18 f on E.out, starting on f4. The ring breathes with a period of 120 f, ±2%. Place it at about 40% of runtime.
- **Use when:** A dark film's single most important promise needs to stop the viewer halfway through.
- **Avoid when:** Light-mode films, films that already alternate dark and light, or when the music has no gap to place it in.

### Theme flip mid-move

`cl-theme-flip-in-motion` · colour and light · signature · energy high · feature, launch, walkthrough

In the middle of a camera fly-over, the dark page and stage flash to their light versions, top first, and the motion never pauses.

- **Build:** Render dark and light versions of the same page as two identical layers on the same moving plane, inside one world container driven by src/lib/camera.ts so they share every transform. Reveal the light layer through mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, black X%, transparent X+30%), with X running from -30% to 100%, so the top bands lead by about 2 f. On the same span, swap the stage from the C.ink grid to the C.paper studio. Keep the camera at cruise speed through the flip: it shows theme support and doubles as the film's dark-to-light act change.
- **Timing:** 6 f in total, with the mask edge on E.linear (frame luma goes about 40, 140, 205, 235). The top leads by 2 f. Leave the camera's own easing untouched.
- **Use when:** Products with dark and light modes, or as the single dark-to-light act transition of a film.
- **Avoid when:** The camera is static (the flip turns into a plain crossfade), or the light version would not match the dark one pixel for pixel.

### Glow and grain boil on held graphics

`dv-living-grain-flicker` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · any

While shapes hold still, their glow and grain change every frame by a few percent, so a held frame never freezes.

- **Build:** Recipe: a set of 4-8 baked grain plates cycled by frame (seeded), at low opacity. Anatomy: Per-frame seeded noise on the grain plate and a tiny lightness wobble. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** Every frame, amplitude 2-4 % luma.
- **Use when:** Any hold longer than about 30 f on a graphic, especially on twos.
- **Avoid when:** Visible flicker (keep it 2-4 % of luma).

### Click or hover lights the object

`dv-interaction-light-response` · micro-interactions · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A click pushes the camera toward the caret and a soft light blooms at the click point; a glossy 3D object brightens and shifts colour under the hovering cursor.

- **Build:** SnapZoom (pre build) on the click; light as SnapZoom flash with a swell (gain 0.4). Anatomy: Push tau about 6.5 f; light attack 13 f, release 23 f; hover 84 f then a 20 f shrink. Sound: A click on the beat (+28 ms); a UI pop on the punch-in. Materials: Emissive heat under the cursor: a glossy object lit by the scene brightens to a hot emissive version of the accent when the cursor reaches it (brightness 1 -> 1.5 and saturation 1.4 over 40 f), its rims glow (drop-shadow 30 px in the accent) and a soft radial glow pools on the ground under it (about 60 % at the centre to 0 at 500 px).
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Materials:** Emissive heat under the cursor: a glossy object lit by the scene brightens to a hot emissive version of the accent when the cursor reaches it (brightness 1 -> 1.5 and saturation 1.4 over 40 f), its rims glow (drop-shadow 30 px in the accent) and a soft radial glow pools on the ground under it (about 60 % at the centre to 0 at 500 px).
- **Conditions:** light built into the device (core, body, falloff), never a uniform halo
- **Timing:** Push 15-20 f; light 36 f.
- **Use when:** The decisive click of a demo; a hover on a hero object.
- **Avoid when:** Halo glows in house films.

### Soft window-blind shadows across the set

`dv-window-light-shadows` · depth and 3d · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Broad soft diagonal shadow stripes (window blinds) fall across a tabletop set and move with it, so the scene reads as a real room.

- **Build:** A baked shadow plate (dither-gradient 'shadow' kind) with stripes, inside the set's transform. Anatomy: Static stripe plate in the ground's hue, multiplied, carried with the set. Sound: None. Materials: One shadow pass unites photographed and drawn pieces: a real photo cut-out lies among flat illustrated stickers and a drawn note, and a single set of soft diagonal window-blind shadows (bands 140-180 px at 1080p, a 60 px gaussian edge, a dark tint of the ground at multiply) crosses all of them, so the photo and the drawings share one room.
- **Primitive:** `fx/KeyLight`
- **Materials:** One shadow pass unites photographed and drawn pieces: a real photo cut-out lies among flat illustrated stickers and a drawn note, and a single set of soft diagonal window-blind shadows (bands 140-180 px at 1080p, a 60 px gaussian edge, a dark tint of the ground at multiply) crosses all of them, so the photo and the drawings share one room.
- **Timing:** Static; moves with the camera.
- **Use when:** Tabletop or desk sets with objects.
- **Avoid when:** Moving the stripes independently of the set.
